# Blitter register trace corpus -- proposal §12's "recorded Workbench
# traces" half of the blitter differential (docs/blitter-differential.md).
# One line per distinct register signature, already deduplicated by
# `crate::blitter_trace::BlitterTrace` at capture time, tagged AREA or
# LINE by which shape replays it (`AreaCase` remaps every pointer into
# this differential's scratch arena; `LineRawCase` keeps every register
# verbatim except BLTCPT/BLTDPT, which are remapped like AreaCase's own
# pointers -- see blitter_trace.rs and blitter_differential.rs for why).
#
# Provenance: `machine-hosted --rom nondistribution/A1200.47.115.rom --hd
# nondistribution/m68k-machine.hdf --blitter-trace <this file> --screenshot
# ... --screenshot-frame 4000 --max-frames 4500` -- the same planar
# Workbench boot this project's baselines are pinned against (752x576, 6
# distinct colours, 13507/433152 non-background pixels at frame 4000,
# unchanged by tracing). Neither the ROM nor the HDF is redistributable
# (nondistribution/README.md), so this file -- derived data, not the
# image itself -- is what's checked in; regenerate by rerunning the above
# with those local, unredistributed inputs.
#
# AREA: 110 area-mode BLTSIZE arms observed, deduplicating to the 30 AREA
# lines below. Every one shares one shape: USED only (BLTCON0 bits 8-11 =
# 0001, no memory-backed source channel) with minterm LF=0xF0 (D = A, so a
# disabled A channel's constant BLTADAT becomes the fill value) --
# graphics.library's plain rectangle-fill idiom, used repeatedly for
# window/icon background clears. They vary only in BLTAMOD/BLTCMOD/BLTDMOD,
# BLTADAT/BLTBDAT, and width/height. Nothing here uses a shifted barrel, a
# non-identity minterm, BLTCON1's fill mode, or more than one active
# channel -- narrower than the randomised half's coverage (256 minterms,
# all 16 channel-enable combinations, full 0-15 shifts). See
# docs/blitter-differential.md for the full discussion.
#
# LINE: 1368 line-mode BLTSIZE arms observed, deduplicating to the 791
# LINE lines below -- far more than area mode contributes (92% of every
# blit this boot armed was a line, not a filled rectangle). Every one of
# the 791 has BLTCPT == BLTDPT at arm time (graphics.library's universal
# convention -- 0 skipped for that reason) and BLTCON0's USEB clear (no
# B-channel texture memory read; the "dashed" pattern register BLTBDAT is
# always the all-ones 0xFFFF, i.e. no dash is actually visible regardless
# of the texture-shift nibble's value). Six distinct minterms appear
# (0x0A, 0x2A, 0x6A, 0xCA, 0xEA, 0xFA -- the task brief's "classic $2A/$EA"
# plus four more), all eight Bresenham octants (SUD/SUL/AUL), SING is set
# on 170 of 791 (~21%), the start-x shift nibble (BLTCON0 bits 12-15) and
# the texture-shift nibble (BLTCON1 bits 12-15) each span the full 0-15
# range, line lengths (BLTSIZE's height field, the pixel count) run 1-43,
# and the row-stride moduli (BLTCMOD, the only modulo `execute_line`
# actually reads for the row step) span several real bitplane widths (2,
# 4, 6, 80 bytes/row). BLTAPTH (the error term's high word, replayed
# verbatim) is nonzero in 8 of the 791 signatures -- leftover state from
# whatever this register held before the arm, not always a clean sign
# extension of the low word, which is exactly why this corpus replays it
# verbatim rather than deriving it. See docs/blitter-differential.md's
# "Recorded Workbench traces" section for the full discussion, including
# how this compares to the randomised half's octant/SING/texture sweep.
#
# columns (AREA): bltcon0 bltcon1 bltafwm bltalwm amod bmod cmod dmod adat bdat cdat width height c_eq_d
# columns (LINE): bltcon0 bltcon1 bltafwm bltalwm blt_apt_h blt_apt_l amod bmod cmod dmod adat bdat cdat width height c_eq_d
# (all decimal; amod/bmod/cmod/dmod signed, width/height are BLTSIZE's raw
# fields with 0 meaning 64/1024 (AREA) or 2/1024 by convention (LINE,
# width unread by execute_line), c_eq_d is 0 or 1 -- see
# crates/machine-hosted/src/blitter_trace.rs and docs/blitter-differential.md)
